rows.name: SLICE_HOSTNAME
rows.section: 2. Dice, Slice and the launcher wrappers

cells.Set by: A person, by hand. Test fixtures set `test`.
cells.Values and default: Any text that is not empty. `bin/slice` uses it as the host name. Unset: the host name of the server, cut at the first dot.
cells.Effect: Changes the name of the log directory `logs-<value>` under the repository root. The directory holds the run logs and the lock file `.slice.lock`. `bin/slice route` prints the value on its `host:` line. `bin/slice` does not check the text. The value becomes part of a directory name.

rows.name: SLICE_MANIFEST_OVERRIDE
rows.section: 2. Dice, Slice and the launcher wrappers

cells.Set by: CI workflows and Slice tests. `bin/slice` forwards it to `--remote` jobs.
cells.Values and default: Path of a JSON file in the format that `ctest --show-only=json-v1` prints. Unset: `bin/slice` runs `ctest --test-dir gen --show-only=json-v1` and uses the output as the test list.
cells.Effect: `bin/slice` reads the test list from the file and does not run `ctest`. The file gives the name, command, labels, working directory and environment of each test. A missing file or invalid JSON ends `bin/slice` with an `error:` line and exit status 1. With `--remote`, `bin/slice` passes the file and the variable to the LSF job. `t/t_slice_catch2_manifest.py` reads the same variable. CI sets it to a file named `ci-test-manifest.json`.

rows.name: SLICE_PLATFORM
rows.section: 2. Dice, Slice and the launcher wrappers

cells.Set by: A person, by hand. Test fixtures set `test`.
cells.Values and default: Any text that is not empty. `bin/slice` uses it as the platform name, for example `genoa96`. Unset: `bin/slice` asks `config/resource-parser.sh` for the server type in `config/resource-map.yaml`. If that fails, the name is `_unknown`.
cells.Effect: Selects the platform block of `config/test-benchmarks.json` that `bin/slice` reads and writes. A platform block holds the benchmark data of one server type. `bin/slice run` exits with an error when the file has no complete block for the name. `bin/ci/bench_refresh_platform.py` ignores the variable and prints the detected server type.

rows.name: SLICE_REPO_ROOT
rows.section: 2. Dice, Slice and the launcher wrappers

cells.Set by: Slice test fixtures. A person can set it by hand.
cells.Values and default: Path of a directory with the layout of the repository root. Unset: the parent directory of the `bin` directory that holds the `bin/slice` script.
cells.Effect: Changes where `bin/slice` finds `config/test-benchmarks.json`, `config/resource-parser.sh`, `config/resource-map.yaml`, `gen/` and `bin/dice`. `bin/slice` also writes its `logs-<host>` directory there. With `--remote`, a value that names a directory other than the checkout of the script ends `bin/slice` with an error and exit status 2. Inside a Dice grant, `bin/slice run` and `bin/slice bench` read `resource-parser.sh` and `resource-map.yaml` from `/opt/positron/config`.

rows.name: SLICE_STATE_DIR
rows.section: 2. Dice, Slice and the launcher wrappers

cells.Set by: Slice test fixtures. A person can set it by hand.
cells.Effect: Changes where `bin/slice` keeps one state file for each `bin/slice` process that runs tests. The files are `<value>/slice-state-<user id>/slice-state-pid<PID>.json`. `bin/slice view`, `bin/slice queue` and the cleanup of stale test processes read them. `bin/slice` creates the per-user directory with mode `0700`. If that directory belongs to another user or keeps another mode, `bin/slice` writes no state file and prints no error. `bin/slice` also reads older files named `slice-state-pid*.json` in `<value>` itself.

hints.problem: Rule 1. "stale" is an uncommon word. In `bin/slice` it means that the owning `bin/slice` process has ended (bin/slice:2942). Original phrase: "the cleanup of stale test processes read them."
hints.suggested: Replace the whole cell with: Changes where `bin/slice` keeps one state file for each `bin/slice` process that runs tests. The files are `<value>/slice-state-<user id>/slice-state-pid<PID>.json`. `bin/slice view`, `bin/slice queue` and the cleanup of test processes whose `bin/slice` process has ended read them. `bin/slice` creates the per-user directory with mode `0700`. If that directory belongs to another user or keeps another mode, `bin/slice` writes no state file and prints no error. `bin/slice` also reads older files named `slice-state-pid*.json` in `<value>` itself.

rows.name: TRON_TEST_CHILD_LIBRARY_PATH
rows.section: 2. Dice, Slice and the launcher wrappers

cells.Values and default: A library search path: directories separated by colons. Unset: `bin/slice` adds nothing to the `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` of the tests it starts.
cells.Effect: `bin/slice` puts the value in front of `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` for each test that it starts. `bin/slice` itself keeps its own `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`. The variable is not passed to the test. `bin/slice` ignores a CTest `ENVIRONMENT` entry with this name. The test log shows the resulting `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` in its `# cmd:` line. In CI, `bin/ci/tron-build/test_runtime.py` writes the variable to the GitHub environment file.

rows.name: DICE_ETA
rows.section: 2. Dice, Slice and the launcher wrappers

cells.Values and default: Seconds as a number of 0 or more, or `inf`, `infinity`, `infty`, or `?` for no estimate. A negative number or other text makes `slice submit` exit with status 2. Unset: `inf`. Dice then expects no end time for the submission.
cells.Effect: Sets the predicted run time that the wrapper passes as `--eta` to `bin/slice submit` when it queues `rinzler` or `runtron` through Dice. The Dice scheduler uses the value to decide whether a later submission can start before an earlier one. The wrapper reads it only on a shared host outside a grant. Dice does not stop a submission that runs longer. `bin/dice-lsf-runner` removes every `DICE_` variable from remote work. A value from the submitting shell does not reach a `--remote` run.

cells.Values and default: Any text. The script does not check it. Unset: the script sends the text `YOUR_API_KEY`.
cells.Effect: `burst-test.sh` (the script that sends a burst of chat completion requests to a server) puts the value in the header `Authorization: Bearer <value>` of every request. The option `-k` or `--key` overrides the variable.

cells.Values and default: Full URL of a chat completions endpoint, including the path. `curl` receives the text unchanged. Unset: `http://localhost:3000/v1/chat/completions`.
cells.Effect: `burst-test.sh` (the script that sends a burst of chat completion requests to a server) posts every request to this URL with `curl`. The option `-u` or `--url` overrides the variable.

cells.Values and default: Whole number of tokens from `1` to `999999999`, without a leading zero. It must be larger than `MAX_TOKENS_JITTER`. Any other value stops the script with exit status 1. Unset: 512 tokens.
cells.Effect: It is the middle of the `max_tokens` range of `burst-test.sh` (the script that sends a burst of chat completion requests to a server). Each request gets a random `max_tokens` from base minus jitter to base plus jitter. The option `-t` or `--max-tokens` overrides the variable. The script header says that long prompt mode needs a server context window of `PROMPT_TOKENS_MAX` plus base plus jitter tokens.

cells.Values and default: Whole number of tokens from `0`, without a leading zero. It must be smaller than `MAX_TOKENS_BASE`. Any other value stops the script with exit status 1. Unset: 128 tokens.
cells.Effect: It is half of the width of the random `max_tokens` range of `burst-test.sh` (the script that sends a burst of chat completion requests to a server). Each request gets a `max_tokens` from base minus jitter to base plus jitter. The value `0` gives every request the base value. The option `-j` or `--jitter` overrides the variable. Above 16383 tokens the range ends below base plus jitter. The bash variable `RANDOM` gives at most 32767.

cells.Values and default: A model name as text. The script does not check it. Unset: `llama-3.2-3b-instruct-fast-tp2`.
cells.Effect: `burst-test.sh` (the script that sends a burst of chat completion requests to a server) puts the value in the `model` field of every request. The option `-m` or `--model` overrides the variable.
